children: Frost's expanded Rockets relationship and first professional women's sports team partnership signals a deeper investment in Houston sports, fans and communities

HOUSTON, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Frost Bank today announced an expanded partnership with the Houston Rockets and a new partnership with the Houston Comets, becoming the Official Bank of both teams. The designation marks Frost's first partnership with a professional women's sports team and expands its longstanding relationship with the Rockets.

The expanded partnership builds on nearly a decade of collaboration with the Rockets, reflecting a shared commitment to creating meaningful fan experiences, investing in Houston communities and supporting the next chapter of sports in one of America's most passionate cities.

As women's sports continue to reach new levels of visibility, fandom and cultural influence, Frost's partnership with the Comets represents a significant milestone for the bank and reinforces its commitment to supporting opportunities that bring people together and strengthen local communities.

"Houston brings together hardworking people, diverse perspectives, and a collaborative spirit that creates opportunities for everyone," said Richard Mann, Frost's Houston region president. "As women's sports continue to gain momentum, our partnership with the Comets and expanded relationship with the Rockets reflects Frost's continued investment in Houston, its fans and its future. Together, we will create meaningful experiences while supporting initiatives that strengthen the communities we serve."
Partnership Highlights
Financial Literacy and Community Impact –

Frost will work alongside both the Rockets and Comets to develop community-focused financial literacy initiatives designed to help more Houstonians build financial confidence and achieve their financial goals.
Frost Fridays Fan Experiences –

Frost will bring its popular Frost Fridays series to select Rockets and Comets home games, featuring unique fan experiences, giveaways, and custom activations designed to engage with fans throughout the season.
Presenting Partner for Tentpole Moments Across Both Leagues –
Frost will serve as a presenting partner of the "For the Cup" series during the NBA Cup and WNBA Commissioner's Cup across Rockets and Comets platforms and fan experiences.
Enhanced Frost Legends Club –
The partnership includes the launch of Frost Legends Club, creating an upgraded experience for guests at Rockets and Comets games and arena events.

"The return of the Houston Comets marks a historic moment for our city, our fans, and the future of women's sports," said Gretchen Sheirr, President of Business Operations. "For many Houstonians, the Comets represent cherished memories and a championship legacy. For a new generation, they symbolize what is possible. We're grateful to Frost for embracing this exciting new chapter and for its continued commitment to our organization. As a longtime Rockets partner and now a founding partner of the Comets, Frost shares our belief in honoring tradition while investing in the future. Together, we look forward to creating exceptional experiences, giving back to our community, and building memories that will inspire Houston for years to come."
Additional partnership and community programming details will be announced throughout the season.

About Frost
Frost is the banking, investments and insurance subsidiary of Cullen/Frost Bankers, Inc. (

), a financial holding company with $53.9 billion in assets at June 30, 2026. One of the 50 largest U.S. banks by asset size, Frost provides a full range of banking, investments and insurance services to businesses and individuals in the Austin, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, Permian Basin, Rio Grande Valley and San Antonio regions. Founded in 1868, Frost has helped Texans with their financial needs during three centuries. For more information, visit FrostBank.com.
About Houston Rockets/Houston Comets

In October 2017, Tilman J. Fertitta assumed ownership of the National Basketball Association's Houston Rockets and operation of the team's home arena, Toyota Center, located in downtown Houston.  In May 2026, the Women's National Basketball Association approved the relocation of the Connecticut Sun to Houston for the 2027 season, marking the return of the Houston Comets.  The Rockets, who originated in San Diego and moved to Houston in 1971, are entering their 60th season as an NBA franchise and won back-to-back championships in 1993-94 and 1994-95.  The Comets were one of the original eight WNBA franchises and won the league's first four championships from 1997-2000.  Through the Clutch City Foundation, the Rockets and Comets utilize the power of basketball to transform lives and positively impact the Houston community.  For more information, please visit Rockets.com and HoustonComets.com.
